acquisition method: raw MS data were acquired in the data-dependent acquisition mode.
alkylation reagent: before the gel pieces were placed in 100 μL of 55 mM iodoacetamide and incubated in the dark for 20 min.
alkylation concentration: before the gel pieces were placed in 100 μL of 55 mM iodoacetamide and incubated in the dark for 20 min.
cleavage agent: digested with 13 ng/μL trypsin (sequencing grade, Promega, USA) in 50 mM NH4HCO3 overnight at 37 °C.
enrichment method: We excised each of the three predominant bands from an IEF gel of urine samples, cut the gel slice into 1 mm3 pieces and transferred them to 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tubes.
fractionation method: IEF was performed in a Bio-Rad model 111 Mini IEF Cell apparatus.
instrument: coupled to a Q-Exactive mass spectrometer through an EASY-Spray nano-electrospray ionization source (Thermo Scientific, USA).
ionization type: coupled to a Q-Exactive mass spectrometer through an EASY-Spray nano-electrospray ionization source (Thermo Scientific, USA).
labeling: The extracted peptides were analysed using an EASY-nLC 1000 system (Thermo Scientific, USA) coupled to a Q-Exactive mass spectrometer through an EASY-Spray nano-electrospray ionization source (Thermo Scientific, USA).
reduction reagent: We rehydrated the gel pieces by incubating them with 100 μL of 10 mM dithiothreitol at 56 °C for 30 min
reduction concentration: We rehydrated the gel pieces by incubating them with 100 μL of 10 mM dithiothreitol at 56 °C for 30 min
